claims.statement: The test suite uses pytest with socket isolation enabled via --disable-socket flag to prevent network calls, configured with verbose output mode, automatic asyncio mode, and function-scoped asyncio fixture loops.

The cross-reference checker scans Markdown below src, skips code-sample snippets and node_modules, ignores fenced code and escaped references, and requires unfenced shared OSS references to resolve in every scope in which the page is built.

The code-sample runner executes eligible Python, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Go, and shell files under src/code-samples; FILES selects an explicit subset, while an unset FILES runs all eligible files excluding __pycache__ and node_modules.

Each executable sample has a 1,200-second default timeout, configurable through CODE_SAMPLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, and runs with language-specific commands and working directories: uv Python, npx tsx, Go, bash, or JBang using Java 21 for Java and Kotlin.

The code-sample workflow skips fork pull requests to protect provider secrets, provisions a PostgreSQL pgvector service and language toolchains, and supplies provider credentials plus POSTGRES_URI to the sample runner.

Scheduled monthly and manually dispatched code-sample workflows run all samples, whereas pull requests test only changed eligible sample files; the job allows 90 minutes for full runs and 60 minutes for pull-request runs.
A sample that remains LangSmith-rate-limited after three attempts separated by 15-second delays is recorded as skipped and does not fail the runner; other unsuccessful samples cause a nonzero exit.

CI regenerates the Python provider overview and fails when the committed generated file differs, directing changes to the generator or packages.yml; only designated automated-update PRs and the bypass-auto-check label skip this check.

Mint export validation deliberately checks external URLs while disabling internal link and hash checks because the export omits a complete page set; it limits external HTTP concurrency to four and timeout to 30 seconds.
When CODE_SAMPLE_TRACING is enabled, successful samples are followed by LangSmith trace collection; a trace collection failure makes the runner exit nonzero even when the sample process passed.

Trace collection only creates a public manifest entry for a single-snippet source file with a qualifying recent agent root run; it records multi-snippet source files as skipped and generated snippet MDX appends a View example trace card only for a manifest URL.

After a successful scheduled or manually dispatched full sample run and snippet regeneration, the workflow opens or updates a chore/refresh-code-sample-traces pull request containing the trace manifest and generated snippet MDX changes.

The local PostgreSQL helper honors POSTGRES_URI before attempting a pgvector testcontainer, Docker, or a default local connection, and its store preparation drops shared store and migration tables before setup.
Reusable test, lint, and documentation-link workflows install the test dependency group with UV_FROZEN enabled, preventing CI from implicitly refreshing the lockfile.
The code-sample Make target installs the Node package environment in src/code-samples before invoking the runner; that package is ESM and declares tsx plus the TypeScript sample dependencies.
The reusable documentation-link workflow builds with Node 22, validates anchors and redirects through make broken-links-with-anchors, then validates the OpenAPI specification.
The focused builder tests verify the supported copy-extension policy, an empty source tree, and that a local TSX snippet component is copied into build/snippets.

Snippet-generation tests preserve embeddings and provider-specific chat model IDs while expanding only eligible agent model strings, and enforce different Python and TypeScript Google provider keys across the sample tree.

The code-snippet tests require both the declared and locked @langchain/google versions to be at least 0.2.6, preventing a stale TypeScript dependency resolution from omitting the Gemini mixed-tool configuration fix.

The LangSmith OpenAPI processor fetches only its allowlisted API host when no local input is supplied, applies public-documentation hiding, title, grouping, and tag-ordering policy, and writes the processed JSON only when invoked with --write.

The trusted daily or manually dispatched LangSmith OpenAPI refresh processes the live specification and opens or updates one chore/refresh-langsmith-openapi review PR only when src/langsmith/langsmith-platform-openapi.json changes.
Autolink preprocessing resolves markers according to the active conditional language scope, preserves regular fenced-code content, and unescapes escaped markers without resolving them.

The changelog assembler reads fragments from a sibling langchainplus checkout by default, refuses ledger paths outside this repository, excludes ledger-listed names, and updates the sorted publication ledger only when --record is used after ready fragments render.

A changelog fragment requires title, body, components, and a ready or held status, with a flag required for held status; held entries are rendered only after an Eppo-backed predicate confirms an active production catch-all allocation has full exposure and one appropriate variation.

The self-hosted changelog enhancement runs only on /langsmith/self-hosted-changelog, indexes visible h2 headings whose IDs are exactly stable minor releases, coalesces route and DOM mutations through requestAnimationFrame, and cleans up generated indexes and heading classes after navigation away.

The reusable CI test job invokes make test, which runs pytest, while the documentation-link workflow uses Node 22 for Mint validation; neither workflow invokes tests/changelog-navigation.test.js, so its Node built-in test command must be run explicitly.
